findings.title: Valve Target Recommendation ships disabled where a mixing valve is set, and available-but-unknown where none is
findings.claim: In 5 of 5 golden topologies with mixing_valve_mode=manual, Valve Target Recommendation publishes a target (23.0 °C) and its reason while its registry default is off; in the same 5 topologies without a valve it is available with state unknown.
findings.mechanism: ValveTargetRecommendationSensor keeps a static _attr_entity_registry_enabled_default=False and the base availability, while the payload key it reads (coordinator._mixing_valve_view) exists only when mixing_valve.is_throttling(mode). Its sibling opt-in readouts take default and availability from the configured feature: ConfiguredInputMixin (ECL110, probes; #1302/#1542) and DHWEntityMixin (#1398). The class docstring's reason ('disabled rather than eternally-unknown') covers only the no-valve install, where the entity is nevertheless available.

evidence.unit: topologies (of 5) with a throttling valve where the entity publishes a value while enabled_default is False
evidence.machine: leads box L2: 4-core Linux cloud container, /home/claude/venv314 CPython
evidence.contention_note: leads fan-out: seats L1/L3/L4 on the same box; count is contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb valve: entity_registry_enabled_default follows mixing_valve.is_throttling(config mixing_valve_mode) (in memory)

findings.metric_definition: Topologies (of the 5 golden coordinator scenarios) with mixing_valve_mode=manual where the entity's native_value is not None and entity_registry_enabled_default is False.
findings.phenomenon_property: An entity whose value exists only under an opt-in configuration feature takes its registry default and its availability from that feature being configured, never from a static class attribute.
findings.seam_rule: grep -n '_attr_entity_registry_enabled_default = False' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/sensor.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/binary_sensor.py  (each hit checked against the payload gate its value needs)
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Gate ValveTargetRecommendationSensor's default and availability on mixing_valve.is_throttling(mode) in the ConfiguredInputMixin shape; update README.md:551/:560 and the disabled-set pins in tests/entities.py. Existing registry entries keep their state.

findings.title: Setup overview page and setup diagram publish English slot text on a Swedish install
findings.claim: With the Swedish translation active, 22 of the 23 text lines the setup_overview flow page renders, all 16 slot labels describe_setup publishes (setup_topology, drawn verbatim by the card) and all 3 sensor_advisor labels are byte-identical to the English install's, while the narrative on the same plan sensors is Swedish (0 of 1 identical).
findings.mechanism: topology._SLOTS holds English literal labels and render_text_summary English headings; describe_setup, render_text_summary and rank_sensor_advisor take no language, so config_flow._setup_overview_form fills the sv template's {setup_summary} with English and the plan sensors publish English labels; narrative.render, by contrast, picks TEMPLATES[language].

evidence.unit: published strings identical en/sv (22 page lines + 16 slot labels + 3 advisor labels)
evidence.machine: L4 leads box: 4-vCPU Linux container, CPython 3.14 (venv314), OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: other leads seats shared the box; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb: the three topology functions wrapped in memory to pass every published literal through a Swedish table when the language is sv (the narrative.render pattern)

findings.metric_definition: published setup strings (rendered setup_overview lines, setup_topology slot labels, sensor_advisor labels) byte-identical between an en and an sv install
findings.phenomenon_property: Every user-facing string the backend publishes for the setup diagram and the sensor advisor follows the instance language, as the narrative does.

null_control.note: narrative.render on the same sensors follows the language

findings.proposed_fix_scope: topology.py: slot labels and summary headings keyed by translation key (resolved from strings/translations by hass.config.language in the flow, or published as keys the card translates); config_flow/sensor call sites pass the language.

findings.title: Grid-fee bounds are SEK numbers: a 0.05 EUR/kWh fee is unenterable in HUF, ISK, JPY and KRW
findings.claim: A 0.05 EUR/kWh transfer fee converted into each of 12 instance currencies draws 8 blocking verdicts across 4 currencies (HUF, ISK, JPY, KRW): the rules text is refused as implausible (HUF, KRW), the fixed-fee field's selector caps it at 5 in any currency (all four), and an entity-mode fee raises the grid_fee_magnitude repair (HUF, KRW); SEK, EUR, NOK and DKK draw 0.
findings.mechanism: grid_fee.IMPLAUSIBLE_FEE_SEK_PER_KWH = 10.0 (read by spec_problem and coordinator._audit_grid_fee) and the grid_fee_fixed NumberSelector max 5 are fixed numbers sized for SEK, while the same widget's unit and the repair text follow hass.config.currency.

evidence.unit: blocking verdicts (3 seams x 12 currencies); 4 currencies
evidence.machine: L4 leads box: 4-vCPU Linux container, CPython 3.14 (venv314), OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: other leads seats shared the box; counts are contention-immune
evidence.tolerance: exact given the stated exchange-rate table

perturbation.change: --perturb: IMPLAUSIBLE_FEE_SEK_PER_KWH 10 -> 1e6 in memory (grid_fee and the coordinator's imported copy)

findings.metric_definition: seam verdicts refusing or capping a 0.05 EUR/kWh fee expressed in each of 12 currencies at a stated rate table (rules refusal, fixed selector max, repair raised)
findings.phenomenon_property: Every magnitude bound on a money field scales with the instance currency the field is labelled in, so a fee that is ordinary in that currency is accepted without a repair.

null_control.note: the currencies the constants were sized for

findings.proposed_fix_scope: grid_fee.py/config_flow.py/coordinator.py: derive the implausibility bound and the fixed-fee selector max from the instance currency (a per-currency scale, or a bound relative to the published spot prices) rather than SEK constants.
